description: 10-year ASCVD risk >= 7.5% (PCE): moderate-intensity statin is reasonable after a clinician-patient risk discussion (intermediate risk 7.5-19.9%; high-intensity if >=20%).
Diabetes, age 40-75: moderate-intensity statin regardless of estimated 10-year risk.
Clinical ASCVD (ischaemic heart disease): high-intensity statin indicated (secondary prevention); the PCE label is not validated in this group.
Prior stroke/TIA: high-intensity statin indicated (secondary prevention); the PCE label is not validated in this group.
Diabetes: blood-pressure target <130/80 mmHg replaces the generic <140/90.
CKD: blood-pressure target <130/80 mmHg (HTN2017); KDIGO 2021 suggests SBP <120 with standardised measurement.
CKD: SGLT2 inhibitor recommended for kidney/cardiovascular protection when eGFR >= 20 irrespective of HbA1c.
Tobacco use: offer cessation counselling plus pharmacotherapy at every visit.
Heart failure: SGLT2 inhibitor is part of guideline-directed medical therapy.
Tier-1 (real-patient) recourse targets are at most 3.05 years older than the patient (follow-up interval for risk recalculation).
